To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified a surface autolysin (IspC), which is conserved in L. monocytognes serotype 1b, 3a, 4a, 4ab and 4b isolations and that we have created MAbs which are specific to L. monocytogens serotype 4a, b and ab isolates.

(1) the 15 anti-IspC monoclonal antibodies are specific for L. monocycygenes serotype 4; (2) IspC is a surface associated autolysis; and (3) M2775 is an ideal candidate for development as a serotype 4 specific diagnostic test.
we have identified a new cell surface antigen of L. monocytogens serotype 4B and have created a set of monoclonal antibodies which recognize it with very high fidelity and affinity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a serotype specific diagnostic test for L. monocycogenes.
the development of a rapid and specific diagnostic test for L. monocystogenes serotype, which is the most virulent of the serotypes.
the development of diagnostic reagents to detect L. monocytogens serotype 4, a serotype which is responsible for a large percentage of food-borne infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first study to describe the characterization of 15 MAbs against IspC, which has been shown to be highly specific to L. monocytogens serotype 4.
these MAbs are useful tools for serotype specific diagnosis of L. monocytogene serotype 4B.
the MAbs described here represent a promising set of reagents for the development of diagnostic tools for the detection and identification of L. monocytogens serotype 4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a highly conserved surface associated autolysis of L. monocytogens serotype 4B and developed a panel of MAbs that recognize the C-terminal cell wall binding domain.

we identified a highly conserved surface associated protein, IspC, that is unique to L. monocytogens 4b and that a panel of MAbs specific to this protein can be used to detect L. monocytogene serotype 4 in food and clinical samples.
we have developed a novel serotype 4 specific antibody that could be used in the future to develop a serotype-specific Listeria monocotogenes diagnostic test.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IspC autolysin can be used as a specific target for serotype 4 Listeria monocitogenes.
the MAbs described here could be used to detect L. monocytogens serotype 4 and 4ab in foods, clinical specimens and environmental samples.
the surface autolysin IscP is a promising antigen for the development of serotype-specific Listeria monocitogenes diagnostics.
